A travel agency sells a “14-year forest getaway” holiday package.
brief: Sell forest life as the ultimate escape from city stress. The brochure promises luxury; the guide keeps revealing the reality. Customers disagree about Wi-Fi, food, comfort, and whether fourteen years is a flexible booking.
roles: Overconfident travel salesperson
Luxury traveller with very high expectations
Budget traveller negotiating every fee
Survival guide who keeps telling the truth
Travel influencer asking about photo opportunities

prompt: Hanuman appears on a podcast about his most unbelievable work assignment.
brief: An epic mission becomes a casual podcast interview. Extraordinary achievements collide with ordinary questions about training, travel expenses, work-life balance, and the sponsor’s product. Let the interruptions get increasingly ridiculous.
roles: Hanuman, treating extraordinary feats as routine
Podcast host desperate for a viral clip
Producer/fact-checker struggling to keep up
Sponsor representative forcing in product mentions
Overenthusiastic caller with unexpected questions

prompt: A customer-service team handles complaints about a flying chariot airline.
brief: A routine complaint desk turns chaotic as passengers question delays, baggage fees, seat upgrades, and the route. Staff try to defend airline policies while the pilot provides explanations that only make things worse.
roles: Customer-service agent trying to remain polite
Pilot with very unhelpful explanations
VIP passenger demanding special treatment
Budget passenger disputing every hidden charge
Travel vlogger broadcasting the whole complaint

prompt: A real-estate agency tries to sell property in Lanka after Hanuman’s visit.
brief: The agency markets a recently damaged property as an incredible opportunity. Every obvious problem becomes a premium feature, while buyers, an inspector, and a local resident reveal what the listing conveniently forgot to mention.
roles: Relentlessly positive real-estate agent
First-time buyer with practical questions
Investor looking for an outrageous bargain
Building inspector refusing to sugarcoat anything
Local resident who knows what really happened

prompt: A vanar sena recruitment drive attracts some very questionable candidates.
brief: The army needs reliable recruits for an enormous mission. Applicants are more interested in remote work, personal branding, or their workout routine. Recruiters must decide who, if anyone, is actually useful.
roles: Recruiter trying to run a professional interview
Commander who needs people who can actually help
Gym enthusiast who turns every task into a fitness challenge
Candidate determined to make the mission fully remote
Influencer applying mainly for the content

Hanuman’s mountain delivery arrives at a Seattle apartment building with very strict HOA rules.
brief: An urgent delivery meets a front desk obsessed with package sizes, parking permits, and quiet hours. Everyone agrees the medicine is important, but nobody agrees where to put the mountain.
roles: Hanuman, the delivery person with no time for paperwork
HOA president defending every building rule
Resident waiting urgently for the delivery
Concierge trying to find space in the package room
Neighbour whose parking spot is now a mountain

prompt: The Ram Setu team holds a project retrospective after successfully shipping a bridge to Lanka.
brief: The bridge is finished, but the retrospective turns into a debate about who deserves credit, why the deadline was impossible, and whether “just one more lane” was in scope. Keep the focus on everyday teamwork chaos.
roles: Project manager determined to call everything a success
Engineer who did the work and kept the receipts
Product manager requesting last-minute features
Quality tester with a very long bug list
Vanar sena customer who just wants to cross the bridge

prompt: The royal calendar invite went wrong. Put these events in story order.
explanation: The wedding comes before the planned coronation and the exile.

prompt: Forest getaway: sort the itinerary from first to last.
explanation: Bharat’s visit at Chitrakoot precedes the later Panchavati episode.

prompt: The golden-deer scam: reconstruct the incident report.
explanation: The deer draws Ram away; Lakshman then leaves before the abduction.

prompt: Ram’s networking journey: order when he first meets these allies in the story.
explanation: Ram meets Jatayu before the abduction, visits Shabari during the search, and meets Hanuman before Sugriva.

prompt: Kishkindha’s leadership shuffle: put the milestones in order.
items: Search parties set out for Sita
Ram and Sugriva form an alliance
explanation: The alliance leads to Vali’s defeat; Sugriva’s reign precedes the search mission.

prompt: Hanuman’s first Lanka trip: sort his status updates.
items: Hanuman finds Sita in Ashok Vatika
Hanuman’s tail is set on fire
explanation: He finds Sita before his capture and the tail-fire episode, then returns with news.

prompt: Lanka launch plan: put these big milestones in order.
items: Hanuman returns with news of Sita
The bridge to Lanka is built
explanation: The scouting report comes before the bridge, crossing, and final victory.

prompt: The homecoming group chat: what happened first?
items: Vibhishan is crowned king of Lanka
explanation: Lanka’s new king is crowned before the return journey and Ram’s coronation.

prompt: Epic binge-watch: arrange these chapters in reading order.
explanation: Ayodhya is followed by the forest book, Kishkindha, and Hanuman’s Lanka mission in Sundara Kanda.

prompt: Season recap in four props: order when these become central to the story.
explanation: Wedding, exile and Bharat’s sandals, the deer episode, then the bridge.
